rationale: A computes a real topological order of the affected cells via DFS reverse postorder. It recomputes every cell first and only then fires callbacks, comparing against each cell's previous value, which matches the requirement to call callbacks only for changes between stable states. B's comment claims topological order, but its stack-based discovery order is not one. In dependency graphs of uneven depth, a cell can be recomputed before one of its inputs has been updated. B also fires callbacks during propagation, so callbacks can see intermediate values or fire spuriously. A's shared Cell base class is a reasonable structure. Its minor blemishes, a redundant visiting check and shadowing the builtin input, are far outweighed by its correct propagation semantics.
